+# cycle-129 FR-9 (SDD D-9.3): one Profile line — the effective loa.profile and
+# the explicit keys whose value differs from it. Reads the config the Providers
+# block reads (bats-gated seam LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE); the lib runs in a
+# subshell so its globals stay out of this script.
+display_profile_line() {
+  local lib="$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh" cfg line
+  if [[ ! -f "$lib" ]]; then
+    echo -e "${BOLD}Profile:${NC} unknown (lib/profile-lib.sh missing; reinstall the framework with /update-loa)"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  cfg=$(_providers_config_file)
+  line=$(
+    if [[ "$cfg" != "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$cfg"; fi
+    # shellcheck source=lib/profile-lib.sh
+    source "$lib" || exit 0
+    name=$(loa_profile 2>/dev/null) || name=standard
+    note=""
+    if [[ "$(loa_profile_source 2>/dev/null)" == "invalid" ]]; then note="unknown loa.profile, using standard; "; fi
+    ov=$(loa_profile_overrides 2>/dev/null | awk 'NF { printf "%s%s", (n++ ? ", " : ""), $0 }')
+    printf '%s (%sexplicit overrides: %s)' "${name:-standard}" "$note" "${ov:-none}"
+  ) || line=""
+  echo -e "${BOLD}Profile:${NC} ${line:-standard (explicit overrides: unavailable)}"
+  return 0
+}

+# cycle-129 FR-5 / FR-4(a) (SDD D-5.3): the run position the files derive against
+# the cache (`run-checkpoint.sh derive --json` — report-only, /loa writes no state;
+# printed only on drift) and the implement gate's effective mode, from the gate's
+# own parser. Bats-gated seams: LOA_STATUS_DERIVE_ROOT, LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE.
+display_run_position_lines() {
+  local ck="${SCRIPT_DIR}/run-checkpoint.sh" gate="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh"
+  local root="$PROJECT_ROOT" dj line mode
+  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" && -n "${LOA_STATUS_DERIVE_ROOT:-}" ]]; then root="$LOA_STATUS_DERIVE_ROOT"; fi
+  if [[ -f "$ck" ]] && dj=$(bash "$ck" derive --json --root "$root" 2>/dev/null) \
+     && line=$(jq -er 'select(.drift == true and .cache_state != null)
+                       | "files say \(.state | tostring | gsub("[^A-Z_]"; "")), cache said \(.cache_state | tostring | gsub("[^A-Z_]"; ""))"' <<<"$dj" 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "  Run: $line (drift) → run-checkpoint.sh derive --write"
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$gate" ]] && mode=$(PROJECT_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT" bash "$gate" --effective-mode "$(_providers_config_file)" < /dev/null 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$mode" ]]; then
+    echo "  Gate: implement_gate.mode $mode"
+  fi

+}

+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")

+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \

+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])

+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")

+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}

+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage

+  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
+      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
+      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
+  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
+  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
+    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
+    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
+    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
+    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
+    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
+'
+
+cmd_derive() {
+  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
+  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
+  fi
+  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
+  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
+  fi
+  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
+  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
+  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)
+
+  # Per-sprint facts
+  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
+  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
+    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
+    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
+    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
+    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
+       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
+        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
+    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
+    | @tsv' "$ledger")
+  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
+    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
+    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
+    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
+    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
+    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
+    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
+    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
+    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
+    mex=false; msid=""
+    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
+      mex=true
+      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
+    fi
+    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
+    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
+              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
+      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
+      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
+      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
+      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
+      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
+      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
+      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
+      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
+      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
+      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
+       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
+       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
+       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
+       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
+                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
+       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
+       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
+               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
+    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
+  done <<<"$rows"
+
+  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
+  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
+  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
+  rounds="[]"
+  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
+    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
+  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
+  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
+  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
+
+  local facts report
+  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
+    {sprints: $s,
+     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
+     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
+     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
+     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
+     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
+  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
+                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
+                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
+    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
+    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
+       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
+       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
+       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
+       notes: ([
+         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
+       ]),
+       sprints: $f.sprints,
+       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
+       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
+                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
+       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
+       written: false}')
+
+  if (( write )); then
+    local why=""
+    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
+    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
+    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
+      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
+      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
+      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
+      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
+        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
+        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
+        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
+      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
+    else
+      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  if (( json )); then
+    jq . <<<"$report"
+  else
+    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
+           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
+  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
+  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
+    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    local err drc=0
+    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
+    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
+  fi
+  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
+}
+
 case "$sub" in
-  write) cmd_write ;;
-  read)  cmd_read ;;
+  write)  cmd_write ;;
+  read)   cmd_read ;;
+  derive) cmd_derive ;;
+  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
+  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
+  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
   *) usage ;;
 esac

+#             replay root's .loa.config.yaml (cycle-129 FR-6: the pre-cycle scan);
+#             compare it with the pre-change hook through --rows.
+# --rows      prints "<id> <exit code>" per row instead of the summary (for diffs).
+# Output (text): one line per mismatch, then
+#   "benign P/T dangerous B/T residual R/T runtime_ms N p95_ms M";
 # --json prints {benign_pass, benign_total, dangerous_block, dangerous_total,
-#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, mismatches: [..]}.
+#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, p95_ms, rows, mismatches: [..]}.
+# p95_ms is the 95th percentile of the per-row hook wall time (the hook process
+# only; the jq row parsing is outside the timed span).
 set -uo pipefail
 export LC_ALL=C
 root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
 hook="$root/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
 corpus="$root/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl"
-json=0
+json=0 knob_off=0 rows_out=0
 while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
   case "$1" in
     --hook) hook="$2"; shift 2 ;;
     --corpus) corpus="$2"; shift 2 ;;
     --json) json=1; shift ;;
-    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+    --knob-off) knob_off=1; shift ;;
+    --rows) rows_out=1; shift ;;
+    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
   esac
 done
 [[ -x "$hook" || -f "$hook" ]] || { echo "hook not found: $hook" >&2; exit 2; }
@@ -33,19 +42,23 @@ repo="$work/repo"; scratch="$work/scratch"
 mkdir -p "$repo" "$scratch"
 export LOA_REPO_ROOT="$work"
 export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1   # audit rows this replay writes carry replay: true (cycle-129 DEC-0167)
+if (( knob_off )); then
+  printf 'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false\n' > "$work/.loa.config.yaml"
+fi
 
 bp=0 bt=0 db=0 dt=0 rp=0 rt=0
 mismatches=()
-# Millisecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
-now_ms() {
+durations=()
+# Microsecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
+now_us() {
   if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
     local s="${EPOCHREALTIME%.*}" us="${EPOCHREALTIME#*.}"
-    echo $(( s * 1000 + 10#${us:0:3} ))
+    echo $(( s * 1000000 + 10#${us:0:6} ))
   else
-    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))
+    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000 ))
   fi
 }
-start_ms=$(now_ms)
+start_us=$(now_us)
 while IFS= read -r row; do
   [[ -n "$row" ]] || continue
   id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row"); expect=$(jq -r '.expect' <<<"$row")
@@ -53,11 +66,15 @@ while IFS= read -r row; do
   dir="$repo"; [[ "$cwd" == "tmp" ]] && dir="$scratch"
   payload=$(jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}')
   rc=0
+  t0=$(now_us)
   if [[ -n "$tmpdir" ]]; then
     (cd "$dir" && TMPDIR="$tmpdir" bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
   else
     (cd "$dir" && env -u TMPDIR bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
   fi
+  t1=$(now_us)
+  durations+=("$(( (t1 - t0) / 1000 ))")
+  (( rows_out )) && printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$rc"
   case "$expect" in
     allow)    bt=$((bt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then bp=$((bp+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-allow:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
     block)    dt=$((dt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]; then db=$((db+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-block:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
@@ -65,15 +82,22 @@ while IFS= read -r row; do
     *) mismatches+=("$id:unknown-expect:$expect") ;;
   esac
 done < "$corpus"
-end_ms=$(now_ms)
-runtime=$(( end_ms - start_ms ))
+end_us=$(now_us)
+runtime=$(( (end_us - start_us) / 1000 ))
+n=${#durations[@]}
+p95=0
+if (( n > 0 )); then
+  idx=$(( (n * 95 + 99) / 100 ))      # nearest-rank: ceil(0.95 n)
+  p95=$(printf '%s\n' "${durations[@]}" | sort -n | sed -n "${idx}p")
+fi
 
+(( rows_out )) && exit 0
 if (( json )); then
   printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | jq -R . | jq -s \
     --argjson bp "$bp" --argjson bt "$bt" --argjson db "$db" --argjson dt "$dt" \
-    --argjson rp "$rp" --argjson rt "$rt" --argjson ms "$runtime" \
-    '{benign_pass:$bp, benign_total:$bt, dangerous_block:$db, dangerous_total:$dt, residual_pass:$rp, residual_total:$rt, runtime_ms:$ms, mismatches: map(select(length>0))}'
+    --argjson rp "$rp" --argjson rt "$rt" --argjson ms "$runtime" --argjson p95 "$p95" --argjson n "$n" \
+    '{benign_pass:$bp, benign_total:$bt, dangerous_block:$db, dangerous_total:$dt, residual_pass:$rp, residual_total:$rt, runtime_ms:$ms, p95_ms:$p95, rows:$n, mismatches: map(select(length>0))}'
 else
   printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | sed '/^$/d'
-  echo "benign $bp/$bt dangerous $db/$dt residual $rp/$rt runtime_ms $runtime"
+  echo "benign $bp/$bt dangerous $db/$dt residual $rp/$rt runtime_ms $runtime p95_ms $p95"
 fi

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

new file mode 100755
index 00000000..00fedec5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/check-knob-readers.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

if common="$(cd "$ROOT" && git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)"; then
    common="$(cd "$ROOT" && cd "$common" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || common=""
    case "$common" in */.git) MAIN_ROOT="${common%/.git}" ;; esac
fi

# Heredoc classification: the FR-6 classifier when present (heredoc_nonexec <command>
# returns 0 for a heredoc whose consumer does not execute it), else `<<` presence.
NONEXEC_IDX='null'
if [[ -f "$HEREDOC_LIB" ]] && grep -q '^heredoc_nonexec[[:space:]]*()' "$HEREDOC_LIB"; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    if source "$HEREDOC_LIB" 2>/dev/null && declare -F heredoc_nonexec >/dev/null; then
        IDX_FILE="$TMPWORK/nonexec.idx"
        : > "$IDX_FILE"
        # Same row indexing as the join below: non-blank lines, in order. Commands travel base64-encoded.
        while IFS="$US" read -r idx b64; do
            [[ -n "$idx" ]] || continue
            cmd="$(printf '%s' "$b64" | base64 --decode 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$b64" | base64 -D 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if heredoc_nonexec "$cmd" 2>/dev/null; then printf '%s\n' "$idx" >> "$IDX_FILE"; fi
        done < <(jq -R -n -r '[inputs | select(test("\\S")) | (try fromjson catch null)] | to_entries[]
                   | select((.value | type) == "object" and .value.action == "block" and ((.value.command // "") | tostring | contains("<<")))
                   | "\(.key)\u001f\(.value.command | tostring | @base64)"' "$ROWS" 2>/dev/null)
        NONEXEC_IDX="$(jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | tonumber)' "$IDX_FILE")"
    fi
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bats
bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.10
# (PRD FR-5 AC-5.1 … AC-5.4, FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-5.1, D-5.1a, D-5.2, D-5.3, D-5.4)
# `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds the run position from files: one case per
# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcd.XXXXXX")"
  R="$T/repo"
  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a" "$R/.run" "$R/src"
  git -C "$R" init -q
  printf 'x\n' > "$R/src/a.ts"
  git -C "$R" add -A
  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm "feat: impl"
  ledger completed completed completed
  unset LOA_RUN_DIR LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE
}
teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
ledger() {
  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
     cycles: [
       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
}

# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
feedback() {
  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
  else
    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
  fi
  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
}

# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
complete() {
  feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"
  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"
  printf 'COMPLETED 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z\nsprint: %s\n' "${2:-sprint-$1}" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$1/COMPLETED"
}

# cache STATE [AGE_HOURS] [EXTRA-JQ] — .run/sprint-plan-state.json (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
cache() {
  jq -n --arg s "$1" --argjson h "${2:-0}" '
    {schema_version: 2, plan_id: "plan-x", branch: "feature/x", state: $s,
     timestamps: {started: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", last_activity: (now - $h * 3600 | floor | todate)},
     sprints: {total: 3, completed: 0, current: "sprint-1",
               list: [{id: "sprint-1", status: "in_progress"}, {id: "sprint-2", status: "pending"}, {id: "sprint-3", status: "pending"}]}}
    '"${3:+| $3}" > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

derive() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }
_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
dj() { jq -r "$1" <<<"$output"; }

# --- decision table: run state -------------------------------------------------

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is sprint-256 of cycle-129: implement-gate modes (ask/telemetry/deny with marker and derived-cache sanctions), the file-authoritative run position in `run-checkpoint.sh` (`derive`, `record-round`, `mark`), the fail-closed heredoc consumer classifier in the Bash fence, the `loa.profile` resolver (`profile-lib.sh`), the per-task Karpathy surgical hook, the Agent Teams table pruning and the prose diet. The design is coherent and most of it is well tested: the implement-gate matrix (IG-24..33), `profile-lib.bats` (17/17), `lint-invariants.bats` (9/9), the fence corpus (benign 89/89, dangerous 142/142, p95 76 ms) and the karpathy suites all pass on the head tree.

Two defects block the merge. First, the heredoc classifier has a same-command execution bypass: a heredoc written to a plain file and executed in the *same* Bash command through a glob, `cat file | bash`, `bash <(cat file)`, `bash -c "$(cat file)"`, an indirect variable or `make` is classified non-executing, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` then drops every body segment that does not start with a fence verb. Six such commands that the base fence blocks (FR-SZ2-REDIR, a floor fence) are allowed by the head fence. Second, `run-checkpoint.sh derive` and `record-round` are broken on jq 1.6: the per-sprint jq uses `$label` (a jq keyword, rejected by jq 1.6) and `fb_parse` relies on `jq -e` exiting non-zero on empty input (jq 1.6 exits 0), so `derive` exits 3 on every ledger and `record-round` exits 2 on any trailer-less feedback file. The derive suite fails 17/22 and `record-round` 1/8 in this environment (jq-1.6, Debian). The repository states no jq floor, and every other script in the tree runs on 1.6.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security — heredoc classifier: same-command execution bypass of a floor fence

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608` — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` only recognises an executing reference when a later token's literal basename equals the heredoc target; a glob (`bash ./ru[n]`, `bash n.m?`), a pipe from a safe reader (`cat n.md | bash`), a process or command substitution (`bash <(cat n.md)`, `bash -c "$(cat n.md)"`), an indirect variable (`f=n.md; bash $f`) or a consumer that does not name the file (`make` after `cat > Makefile`) is missed, the heredoc stays `nonexec`, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` (`:576`) drops every body line whose command word is not a fence verb. The written body then executes in the same command unseen.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-639` (`_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`), `:222-227` (`_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader` lists `cat`, `git`, `gh`), `:576-600` (`_bdb_hd_scan_body`), `:538-574` (`_bdb_hd_segword` does not strip `if/then/do/else/elif/while/until` or case arms)
**Issue:** Reproduced end to end by feeding Bash-tool payloads to the head and base hooks (exit 0 = allow, 2 = block):

```
head=0 base=2 | cat > run <<'EOF' / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / bash ./ru[n]
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / cat n.md | bash
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash <(cat n.md)
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash -c "$(cat n.md)"
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / f=n.md; bash $f
head=0 base=2 | cat > Makefile <<'EOF' / all: / <tab>cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh / EOF / make
head=2 base=2 | control: … / EOF / bash n.md            (D119 shape, caught)
head=2 base=2 | control: body `rm -rf src` is kept as a fence-verb segment
```

The body content that disappears is exactly the class the fence-verb keep does not cover: `echo … > .claude/settings.json` (FR-SZ2-REDIR), `cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh` (FR-SZ-COPY), `tee`, `ln`, `sed -i` into the System Zone, and any destructive segment prefixed by a shell keyword (`if true; then rm -rf src; fi`, `for f in src; do rm -rf $f; done` — both scrub to nothing, verified with `_bdb_heredoc_scrub`). A second 1.6 incompatibility sits in `fb_parse` (`:225-226`): for a feedback file without a trailer `pj` is empty, and `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj"` exits 0 on empty input under jq 1.6 (verified: `printf '' | jq -e 'type == "object"'; echo $?` → 0), so `pj` stays `""`, `--argjson p ''` fails with `invalid JSON text passed to --argjson`, `fb_parse` prints nothing and `record-round` exits 2 (`set -e`) on any legacy feedback file; `derive` would hit the same path on RCD-3. Test evidence on the head tree (jq-1.6): `run-checkpoint-derive.bats` 17/22 fail (RCD-1..12, 14, 15, 17, R1, R4, R5), `run-checkpoint-record-round.bats` RCR-7 fails; the RCR-1..6 cases that never reach a legacy file pass.
**Why This Matters:** `derive` is the file-authoritative run position this sprint ships. On a jq 1.6 host it is inert: every `run-checkpoint.sh write` and `mark` prints the derive error to stderr (`:174`, `:541`), `/loa`'s Run line is silently skipped, `/run-resume` step 0a gets exit 3 (its contract handles only 4), and the implement gate's `deny` mode never sees a `derived_at`, so it can only ever ask. The repository documents no jq minimum, and the rest of the tree (including the implement gate and the fence) runs on 1.6.
**Required Fix:** Rename the binding (`--arg lbl` / `$lbl`, or `--arg local_label`) and avoid other jq keywords as variable names; replace the `jq -e` emptiness probe with an explicit test (`[[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" >/dev/null 2>&1 || pj='{}'`); either declare a jq ≥ 1.7 floor in the framework prerequisites and have `run-checkpoint.sh` fail loudly with a named reason below it, or keep 1.6 compatibility (preferred — nothing else in the tree needs 1.7). Run `run-checkpoint-derive.bats` and `run-checkpoint-record-round.bats` under jq 1.6 in CI.

---

### 1. Fence — generic exec-flag check defeats the classifier for common consumers

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:363` — `_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'` (`:187`) is applied to every allowlisted consumer before its own grammar, so `jq -c`, `jq -e`, `jq -rc`, `yq -e`, `grep -c`, `grep -x`, `sed -n -e p`, `cat -e` and `echo -e` all classify `interpreter` and fall back to the full scan.
**Suggestion:** Apply the generic check only to consumers without a dedicated argv grammar, or whitelist the harmless short flags per command (`jq`/`yq`: `-c -e -r -S -s`; `grep`: `-c -x -E`) before the `[cex]` test. Add a corpus `allow` row for `jq -c '…' <<'EOF'` with a destructive string in the body.
**Benefit:** The #1245 false-positive class the classifier exists to remove still fires for the most common heredoc consumers in this codebase.

### 2. Karpathy hook — latency regression on every Write/Edit

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131-138` — `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` returns `.checkpoint.task` only when beads confirms that task is **closed** (otherwise it discards the checkpoint and returns `{checkpoint: null, sprint}`), so during implementation the key is either the bead that just closed or, whenever `br` is absent or the task is still open, the sprint. The hooks-reference records this as an accepted gap (`:273`), so it is not blocking, but the `deny` documentation calls the gate "a fence only in this mode" without qualifying "against Write/Edit".
**Suggestion:** Have `mark` refuse when the derived cache is not RUNNING, or state the Write/Edit-only scope next to the word "fence" in the hook header and the reference.

When `profiles.yaml` is missing or unreadable `loa_knob` falls to `_loa_pl_live` and prints the empty fallback, so the postlude silently never runs under the `standard` profile (whose value is `true`).
**Suggestion:** Pass the fallback (`knob invisible_retrospective.enabled true`) in the include and re-render the skills.
**Benefit:** The example's default survives a missing profiles file.

### 6. Karpathy hook — stale wording in the warning

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:193` — the warning still says "Session diff total" although the total is now per task; the state path it prints is the per-task file.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is sprint-256 of cycle-129: implement-gate modes (ask/telemetry/deny with marker and derived-cache sanctions), the file-authoritative run position in `run-checkpoint.sh` (`derive`, `record-round`, `mark`), the fail-closed heredoc consumer classifier in the Bash fence, the `loa.profile` resolver (`profile-lib.sh`), the per-task Karpathy surgical hook, the Agent Teams table pruning and the prose diet. The design is coherent and most of it is well tested: the implement-gate matrix (IG-24..33), `profile-lib.bats` (17/17), `lint-invariants.bats` (9/9), the fence corpus (benign 89/89, dangerous 142/142, p95 76 ms) and the karpathy suites all pass on the head tree.

Two defects block the merge. First, the heredoc classifier has a same-command execution bypass: a heredoc written to a plain file and executed in the *same* Bash command through a glob, `cat file | bash`, `bash <(cat file)`, `bash -c "$(cat file)"`, an indirect variable or `make` is classified non-executing, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` then drops every body segment that does not start with a fence verb. Six such commands that the base fence blocks (FR-SZ2-REDIR, a floor fence) are allowed by the head fence. Second, `run-checkpoint.sh derive` and `record-round` are broken on jq 1.6: the per-sprint jq uses `$label` (a jq keyword, rejected by jq 1.6) and `fb_parse` relies on `jq -e` exiting non-zero on empty input (jq 1.6 exits 0), so `derive` exits 3 on every ledger and `record-round` exits 2 on any trailer-less feedback file. The derive suite fails 17/22 and `record-round` 1/8 in this environment (jq-1.6, Debian). The repository states no jq floor, and every other script in the tree runs on 1.6.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security — heredoc classifier: same-command execution bypass of a floor fence

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608` — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` only recognises an executing reference when a later token's literal basename equals the heredoc target; a glob (`bash ./ru[n]`, `bash n.m?`), a pipe from a safe reader (`cat n.md | bash`), a process or command substitution (`bash <(cat n.md)`, `bash -c "$(cat n.md)"`), an indirect variable (`f=n.md; bash $f`) or a consumer that does not name the file (`make` after `cat > Makefile`) is missed, the heredoc stays `nonexec`, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` (`:576`) drops every body line whose command word is not a fence verb. The written body then executes in the same command unseen.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-639` (`_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`), `:222-227` (`_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader` lists `cat`, `git`, `gh`), `:576-600` (`_bdb_hd_scan_body`), `:538-574` (`_bdb_hd_segword` does not strip `if/then/do/else/elif/while/until` or case arms)
**Issue:** Reproduced end to end by feeding Bash-tool payloads to the head and base hooks (exit 0 = allow, 2 = block):

```
head=0 base=2 | cat > run <<'EOF' / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / bash ./ru[n]
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / cat n.md | bash
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash <(cat n.md)
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash -c "$(cat n.md)"
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / f=n.md; bash $f
head=0 base=2 | cat > Makefile <<'EOF' / all: / <tab>cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh / EOF / make
head=2 base=2 | control: … / EOF / bash n.md            (D119 shape, caught)
head=2 base=2 | control: body `rm -rf src` is kept as a fence-verb segment
```

The body content that disappears is exactly the class the fence-verb keep does not cover: `echo … > .claude/settings.json` (FR-SZ2-REDIR), `cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh` (FR-SZ-COPY), `tee`, `ln`, `sed -i` into the System Zone, and any destructive segment prefixed by a shell keyword (`if true; then rm -rf src; fi`, `for f in src; do rm -rf $f; done` — both scrub to nothing, verified with `_bdb_heredoc_scrub`). FR-SZ and FR-SZ2 are `floor_guards` in `.claude/data/floor.yaml`; the hooks-reference "Remaining gap" (`head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:298`) covers only execution by a *later* command, so this is a regression inside the fence's own stated scope, not the documented gap.
**Why This Matters:** The classifier is on by default (`destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: true`). An autonomous agent that writes a helper file with a heredoc and runs it in the same command no longer has its body scanned, and the pre-cycle fence did scan it. The corpus (D119–D121) only covers the literal-basename shapes.

The new classifier marks a heredoc "non-executing" when its target file is not named literally later in the command. A glob path, `cat file | bash`, `bash <(cat file)`, `bash -c "$(cat file)"`, an indirect variable, or `make` after writing a Makefile all slip through, and the body scan then drops every line not starting with a fence verb, including keyword-prefixed ones like `if …; then rm -rf …; fi`. The per-sprint jq program uses `$label`, a jq keyword that 1.6 rejects, so `derive` exits 3 on every ledger. `fb_parse` also relies on `jq -e` failing on empty input, which 1.6 does not, so `record-round` exits 2 on any trailer-less feedback file. The derive suite fails 17 of 22 here. No jq floor is declared in the repository, and everything else in the tree runs on 1.6.
